recipe.title: Steakhouse Filet & Loaded Baked Potato
recipe.summary: Tender filet marinated with soy sauce and Kinder's steak seasoning, served with a Greek-yogurt loaded baked potato and seasoned broccoli for about 40 grams of protein and 400 calories.
recipe.story: This is my lighter steakhouse dinner for nights when I want a really good filet without turning dinner into an all-day project. The soy sauce and Kinder's steak seasoning give the filet plenty of flavor, while plain nonfat Greek yogurt makes the baked potato creamy without needing a heavy topping.
ingredients: 1/4 cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt, such as Kirkland or Chobani
100 grams broccoli florets, about 1 heaping cup
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Marinate the filet with the soy sauce and Kinder's steak seasoning while the oven or grill heats.
Bake the potato until tender, then weigh out a 100-gram portion for the plate.
Grill or pan-sear the filet to your preferred doneness. Let it rest for 5 minutes, then portion 3.5 ounces cooked.
Steam or roast the broccoli until crisp-tender and season with salt and black pepper.
Split the baked potato and top it with the butter, plain nonfat Greek yogurt, salt, and black pepper.
Serve the filet with the loaded baked potato and broccoli.
tips: Weigh the filet after cooking for the closest match to the listed nutrition.
A small potato portion leaves enough room for butter and Greek yogurt while keeping the full plate near 400 calories.
Marinating time can be as short as 10 minutes or up to several hours in the refrigerator.
Nutrition is approximate and will vary with the filet's trimming, the soy sauce, and the exact yogurt used.
